notes.title: AN EFFICIENT GENTLEMAN
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45126080/dd0b179cd07e70ef60f4b7a28d9333ce5f1d238f.png"][/img][/p][h2]Balance Changes[/h2][p][/p][p]We’ve been collecting data on the disputes going on over the past month or so, and noticed that average round lengths have gone up quite a bit since a few patches ago. Our goal is for a 5-gentlemen dispute to 5 wins to be over in about 30 minutes or less on average (depends, of course, on how much of a blowout it is). In our playtests, in the current demo, such disputes can go on for 40 minutes or longer![/p][p][/p][p]To help make things go a bit faster, we’ve done a near blanket buff of damage and increased item spawn rates.[/p][p][/p][h3]Damage Buffs[/h3][list][*][p]Bear Trap 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Bat 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Grenade 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Rocket 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Shotgun 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Oil Barrel (explosion) 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]C4 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Jetpack (scales with distance) 10 → 12[/p][/*][*][p]Champagne bottle 5 → 6[/p][/*][*][p]Airplane, Bicycle 5 → 6[/p][/*][*][p]Shark 5 → 10[/p][/*][*][p]Train 25 → 30[/p][/*][*][p]Molotov (damage per tick) 2 → 3[/p][/*][*][p]Flamethrower (damage per tick) 2 → 4[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]The flamethrower has received a particularly strong buff, with each doing 4 damage per fire tick over 3 seconds. Also, the flamethrower now extends the duration of its burn by holding on adversaries for longer, allowing a very high damage ceiling - so make sure you get out of there quick![/p][p][/p][p]We’ve also added UI explaining that the flamethrower can be ended early by leaping.[/p][p][/p][h3]Item Spawn Rate[/h3][p][/p][p]Item spawn rates have been increased by about 20% across the game, and we made the spawn rate about equal for all player numbers. We originally had much lower spawn rates for fewer player counts, but this ended up not having the desired effect in practice.[/p][p][/p][p]We’ve also significantly increased the max item pedestals that can be around at once, especially for larger maps (Islands now can have twice the number of pedestals at once).[/p][p][/p][p]At the beginning of the round, many item pedestals will be spawned very quickly to help fill out the map before returning to their determined spawn rate, which also should help get rounds started much faster.[/p][p][/p][p]We’re looking forward to hearing feedback on these changes![/p][p][/p][h3]Bug Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed bicycle hit sound only playing for hosts[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed various issues with slapping and throwing in quick succession[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a rare issue where pedestals would stop spawning items after playing many rounds[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bug preventing overhead UI from being visible on notes.title: Bugfixes and Hosting
notes.notes:
[h2]Balance Changes[/h2]

- Changed Hot Hands to function more similarly to Bad Influence, having a chance to activate instead of always activating.

[h2]Major Bugfixes[/h2]

- Addressed issue where the character controller would occasionally run multiple times per tick, causing players to move much faster than they should.

[h2]Changes to Hosting[/h2]

With all of the new players who joined during next fest, our server hosting costs were starting to get out of control. We've done a ton of optimization on both the client and server to mitigate this.

In the process of optimizing the game to reduce our server costs, we noticed that hosting without a dedicated server (using Steam Networking to host on a player's machine) is now often a better experience than using a dedicated server, especially in later rounds when you the game gets really chaotic.

By default the hosting will now run the server locally, but you can still choose to use a dedicated server in the host settings menu. 

In general, you will have a better experience hosting yourself (without a dedicated server) if you have a reliable internet connection and a decently powerful PC, especially if the people you are playing with are in the same region.


[h2]Known Issues[/h2]

We are aware of some rendering issues related to Auto HDR and Apple Silicon machines, usually manifesting as everything being gray or washed out. We are working on addressing those as soon as possible.

notes.title: A SMOOTH GENTLEMAN
notes.notes:
[h1]Another update is here![/h1]

[h2]Major Changes[/h2]

- Restored classic ragdoll jump with improved physics and netcode

Like all things related to movement, this one may be controversial depending on how you liked to use the jumping mechanic. We feel the classic ragdoll jump (with improved physics and netcode so its not as janky as it was before) is closest to the heart of what AGD means to us and to players, and is just way more funny and fun to watch than a more traditional jump.

Of course, this also means that it will be much less precise of a movement tool as the old one was. However, as we move through updates this month, we'll be tweaking the force of the jump and adding perks and upgrades to allow the jump to stay the most fun it can be.

- Changes to lighting and art style

We've spend a lot of time this week iterating on the lighting and color balance in response to player feedback and our own. In general the game should be simpler to look at, less bright, and generally should look more appealing and easy to play and watch.

[h2]Minor Changes[/h2]

- Increased base movement speed
- Many small balance changes

On top of all this we've also got a ton of bug fixes and performance improvements.

Special thanks to our playtesters in our discord https://discord.gg/PTvpYGmtGK for helping us iron out this version before release!

notes.title: The Chaos Update Has Been Released!

[h2]Hello Everyone! A major update has just been released![/h2]

[u]See the full list of changes at the bottom of this announcement. [/u]

While we made a ton of technical and visual improvements in the major update last month, there were a few aspects that felt like a bit of a step back, and that mainly manifested in the feedback that the game had slowed down.

This update is designed to address that, and restore some of the [u]chaos, speed, and insanity of the original demo version[/u]. Perhaps even going... further beyond...

[h3]What's New?[/h3]
We've eliminated the windup times for the jetpack, shotgun, and rocket launcher. We've restored the shark Rufus back to his former ever-present self, biting you as soon as you get too deep in the water. We've removed the caps on Extra Traps and Bigger Traps.

We've permanently included the C4 and Jetpack in the demo and [b]added two new items[/b] that were previously locked, the Champagne Bottle and the Airstrike.

The biggest change is [b]a complete rework of the leap mechanic[/b]. The new leaping is much more controllable and no longer turns you into a ragdoll. We've had a ton of fun working on this change and we hope you enjoy it as much as we did. We're looking forward to your feedback on this change since its probably the biggest gameplay change we've made since the demo was first made public.

There are also a ton of technical, sound, and performance improvements included in this update.

[h3]Community Events & What's Next[/h3]
[u]This Saturday at 4pm EST will be holding an event with the whole dev team in our discord to play with everyone here and hear your feedback on the latest update.[/u] Join the server here: https://discord.gg/E8BP3yWV2u
